title: The Day of the Mud Boot Treaty
skyStory: A quarter-lit moon is drifting through Pisces like a rowboat nobody bothered to tie up. It hums sea shanties under its breath and keeps losing the chorus. Mars wants to steer. Saturn insists on reading the tide chart first, out loud, with footnotes. Below them, every driveway in Atlantic Canada has turned to pudding, and the moon considers this a personal achievement.

reading: May arrives with mud up to the ankles and the Fire Tiger is thrilled about it. You will want to start a garden, a shed, a podcast and a backyard choir before noon. The [[Knight of Wands]] clears its throat. One. Pick the shed, or better, pick the boot rack by the cabin door that has been a pile of boots since March.

Around 4:40 pm a neighbour will offer to help with something you were going to do alone. This is the test. The Tiger's instinct is to say no thanks, I've got it, while carrying eleven things. Say yes instead. Hand over the lightest thing. Watch how nobody falls over and the sky stays exactly where it was.
joel.mission: Scrape the mud off one pair of boots completely, then line them up by the door like they are reporting for duty.
joel.omen: A robin tugging a worm that will not come loose. Patience wins today; let things come out at their own speed.
joel.stoneWhy: grounding for a very muddy day

reading: The Pisces moon is wading in your favourite water today, the shallow kind by the shore where the stones are warm on top and cold underneath. Your intuition is running at full Life Path 11 strength, so trust the first odd feeling of the morning. It knows something about the afternoon.

At some point a small plan will wobble: a message arrives late, a meeting slides an hour. The Wood Rat in you will see the new shape before anyone else does, and you will quietly rearrange three things so the whole day lands softer. Nobody will notice. That is the point, and also slightly annoying. Tell one person what you did.
nancy.mission: Find the muddiest patch on your walk and step around it with exaggerated ballet form, arms included.
nancy.omen: A weathervane pointing the opposite way from the wind. Someone is about to ask your advice; give them the short version.
nancy.elementWhy: Pisces moon, high tide in you

together.text: Each of you photograph the most heroic puddle you can find today and send it without comment. The other must name it like a lake on an old map. Bonus point for anything that ends in Reach, Narrows or Lesser Sorrow.

title: The Day the Peepers Started
skyStory: The moon is down to a sixteen percent sliver and still in Pisces, soaking its feet in a tidal pool and refusing to get out. It has decided tonight belongs to the spring peepers, those thumb-sized frogs who shriek like tiny car alarms from every ditch. The moon is their manager. Saturn has asked for a quieter booking. The request has been denied.

reading: Your voice carries further than usual today, Life Path 3. Something you say in passing, half a sentence while pouring coffee, will lodge in somebody's head and stay there until June. Choose the half sentence carefully. Or don't. The universe likes it when you improvise.

The afternoon brings a pileup of small requests, each one polite, each one wanting a piece of you. The [[Six of Pentacles]] reversed is lurking by the photocopier. Give to two of them. Let the third one wait until tomorrow, and notice that the world keeps turning even when you say later.
joel.mission: Tonight, step outside after dark and count the frog voices for one full minute. Report the number to Nancy, rounded wildly up.
joel.omen: A song stuck in your head with the wrong words. Keep the wrong words; they are a message meant for you.

reading: Here is a quiet day with a secret folded into it. The Wood Rat wakes early, notices the light has shifted further north on the kitchen wall, and files that away as evidence. Spring is negotiating in good faith. You are the only one reading the fine print.

Someone will try to rush you before lunch. Smile, keep your pace, finish the sentence you were on. The [[Six of Swords]] wants you rowing at your own tempo, not theirs. By three o'clock the rusher will be asking you what comes next, because you are the one who actually knows.
nancy.mission: Leave one window cracked an inch this evening and listen for the frogs while you do something ordinary.
nancy.omen: A pair of mismatched mittens still hanging on a hook. Winter is saying goodbye; wave back.
nancy.elementWhy: a soft day with soft focus

together.text: Tonight at the same minute, say 9:17, both of you step outside and listen. Frogs, wind, a far-off dog, a car door. Text each other the strangest sound you heard. The peepers will be judging the entries, and they are tough critics.

title: The Moon Moves Into the Cabin
skyStory: Big news on the cosmic street: the moon has packed its ten percent of light into a duffel bag and moved into Aries, Joel's sign. It knocked on the cabin door, did not wait for an answer, and is now sitting by the woodstove eating Mars's crackers. Mars is delighted. Saturn has sent a strongly worded postcard from Capricorn.

reading: The moon is a houseguest in your sign and it has opinions about your furniture. Expect an urge to rearrange something big: a desk, a shelf, the order of an entire week. Go ahead, but only one room. The [[Knight of Wands]] is guarding the other rooms with a broom.

Your fire runs hot and bright today, which makes you excellent company and slightly hazardous to anyone's to-do list. Somebody will catch your enthusiasm and run off with it like a dog with a glove. Before bed, write down the one idea you most want to chase this month. Fold the paper twice. Tuck it under the onyx.
joel.mission: Move exactly one piece of furniture, even a lamp, six inches to the left and see if anyone notices.
joel.omen: A red truck idling at a stop sign longer than it needs to. It says go, but finish your thought first.
joel.stoneWhy: Nancy's steady stone under all that fire

reading: With the moon off visiting Joel's sign, you get the rare feeling of watching fireworks from across the bay. Everything loud happens over there. You get the glow without the smoke, and a front-row seat to see how it all lands.

Use the quiet. There is a story you have been half-telling for weeks, the one with the woman at the hardware counter and the jar of brass hinges. Today it finds its ending. Tell it to someone new and watch your hands do the work. If they ask what happened next, pause for three full seconds first.
nancy.mission: Send Joel one sentence of encouragement that contains the word tiger and absolutely no other context.
nancy.omen: A kite tangled in a tree. Something you let go of earlier is fine where it landed; leave it there.
nancy.stoneWhy: fire is in the air today
nancy.elementWhy: the steady shore while Aries blazes

together.text: Joel, aim the Aries moon at one shared idea and send Nancy the first step in under twenty words. Nancy, reply with the one question that makes it better. That's it. Two messages, one plan, zero meetings.

title: The Day of the Two Blue Umbrellas
skyStory: A four percent eyelash is all that remains of the moon, still lounging in Aries and still eating the crackers. It has decided to spend its last light on mischief. Somewhere tonight two things that should never match will match perfectly, and the moon will claim it planned the whole thing. Saturn checks the paperwork. The signature is in crayon, but it is valid.

reading: Something odd is lined up for you around 11:20. You will think of a word you have not said in years, maybe periwinkle, maybe gazebo, and within the hour someone will say it out loud in a completely unrelated sentence. Don't even scream. Just raise one eyebrow, slowly, like a detective in the rain.

The Aries moon is still sprawled across your couch, so your energy stays high but scattered. Take a breath before you answer anything with an exclamation point. The [[Eight of Swords]] reversed reminds you that most cages today are just tape on the floor. Step over them.
joel.mission: Pick an odd word right now and drop it into one conversation today without explaining yourself.
joel.omen: Two strangers carrying matching blue umbrellas on a dry day. You and Nancy are about to think the same thought.
joel.stoneWhy: a clear signal through the noise

reading: Your Life Path 11 is buzzing like a porch light full of moths. Little patterns jump out: a licence plate with your birthday digits, the same song in two different shops, a cat in a window that looks exactly like a cat from grade four.

Write them down as they come. By supper you will have a list of three, and the third will connect to something Joel says tonight in a way that makes you both put your phones down and stare at the ceiling. The Wood Rat saw it coming, of course. The Wood Rat always sees it coming.
nancy.mission: Keep a tally of every coincidence you notice today on a sticky note, and send Joel the final count.
nancy.omen: A delivery van with your initials painted on the side. Not a sign. Okay, a little bit a sign.

together.text: ΔΕΣ is on the menu. Before bed, each of you write down the strangest match of the day, then reveal at the same moment. If they connect, you owe the moon a thank-you wave out the window. If they don't, wave anyway. It worked hard.

title: The Seed Packet Summit
skyStory: New moon in Taurus, and the sky has gone dark on purpose, like a theatre before the curtain. Taurus is the gardener of the zodiac, slow and stubborn and very sure about soil. Tonight it is passing out invisible seed packets to anyone who holds out a hand. Mars wants the fast-growing kind. Saturn wants the kind that takes three years and is worth it.

reading: A new moon in an earth sign is a gentle shove toward the slow thing. You know the one: it isn't flashy, it won't go viral, it just quietly makes everything else easier. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] is standing at the cabin fence holding a shovel and not saying a word. He doesn't have to.

Plant one intention tonight. Say it out loud, then say it shorter, then say it in five words. The five-word version is the real one. Write it on the inside of a cupboard door where only you and the mugs will see it. The mugs are excellent at keeping secrets.
joel.mission: Write your five-word intention inside a cupboard door in pencil, small enough that only you know it is there.
joel.omen: A worm crossing the sidewalk after rain. Slow progress is still progress; give it room.
joel.elementWhy: Taurus wants soil under your nails

reading: Your Capricorn bones love an earth new moon. It's like the universe finally speaking your native language, the one with fewer exclamation points and more five-year plans. Settle in. The day moves at the pace of a slow-simmered pot.

A small decision will ask for your attention around 2 pm: which of two things to tend first. Pick the one that will matter in August. The [[Seven of Pentacles]] is leaning on a garden rake nearby, nodding. Later, someone will thank you for a thing you did in March and forgot about. Accept it with both hands.
nancy.mission: Go outside, pick up one smooth stone, and keep it in your pocket until the moon is full again.
nancy.omen: Fog lifting off a field by mid-morning. Something unclear becomes obvious before the day is out.
nancy.stoneWhy: an earth stone for an earth moon

together.text: Each of you plant something tonight, an actual seed in a cup or one word on a scrap of paper. Send the other a photo. Do not check on it for a week. The new moon is watching to see who peeks first.

title: The Darkest Sky of May
skyStory: Zero percent. The moon has switched itself off entirely and is napping in a hammock strung between the horns of Taurus. It's the darkest night of the month, and the stars have rushed in to fill the space like kids into an empty gym. Saturn is pretending to supervise. Mars is already organising a game of tag across the Milky Way.

reading: No moon means no spotlight, and the Fire Tiger behaves differently in the dark. Quieter. More watchful. Today you'll notice what you usually rush past: the crack in the sidewalk shaped like a lightning bolt, the coworker who always arrives first and never mentions it.

Say thank you to that early bird. Specifically. Name the thing. Then accept their awkward shrug without filling the silence. Tonight, if the sky is clear, step outside and find one star you can see from the cabin window every night this month. Name it something ridiculous. It's yours now.
joel.mission: Thank someone today for a specific thing they do quietly, using at least one exact detail.
joel.omen: A streetlight that flickers off as you pass under it. You're about to notice something everyone else misses.

reading: Dark moon, sharp eyes. The Wood Rat was built for exactly this kind of night, and so were you. A puzzle that has been sitting on your desk, or in your head, finally shows you its seams.

Pull one thread around mid-afternoon and the whole thing unravels in a satisfying way. Don't announce it yet. Sit with the solution overnight like a cat on a warm laptop. Tomorrow, when you explain it, your hands will draw a little map in the air, and whoever is listening will follow every turn of it.
nancy.mission: Before bed, turn off every light in one room and sit in the dark for three minutes, just noticing.
nancy.omen: A spider web strung across a doorway. You're closer to the answer than you think; mind the last thread.
nancy.stoneWhy: one clear point in the dark

together.text: No missions tonight, only stars. If it's clear, each of you look up at 10 pm and find the brightest light in the sky. Agree it's the same one even if it obviously isn't. That's how friendship astronomy works, and the dark moon approves.

title: The Day of Two Conversations at Once
skyStory: The moon has rolled out of its Taurus hammock and tumbled into Gemini, the sign of twins, gossip and talking with your mouth full. It is still only two percent lit, but it's already chatting with everyone. Mars has been told the same secret twice by two different stars. Saturn has started taking minutes, in triplicate.

reading: Gemini moon plus Life Path 3 is a lot of talking. Delightful talking. You will be the person in every room who connects two people who should have met years ago. Somebody will say, wait, how do you know everyone? Shrug mysteriously.

The catch is that your attention will split like a river around a rock. Halfway through one sentence you will start another. The [[Two of Wands]] wants you holding two plans with steady hands, not juggling seven. When you catch yourself starting a third thing, finish the first. Out loud. Even if it's just to the kettle.
joel.mission: Introduce two people today, in person or by message, who you think would really like each other.
joel.omen: Two crows arguing on a fence. Someone's about to ask you to settle a debate; pick the funnier side.

reading: You will hear the same piece of news from two different directions today, and the versions won't match. Delicious. The Wood Rat loves a discrepancy. You'll spot exactly where the story bent and why.

Don't correct anyone. Just ask one gentle question that lets the truth float up on its own, like a bubble from the bottom of a tidal pool. It's a storyteller's trick and you're the best at it. Later, around 7, a friend will call with a story so long that you put the kettle on twice. Worth every minute.
nancy.mission: Tell the same short story to two different people today and notice which details you change.
nancy.omen: A bird singing two different songs from the same branch. Both versions are true; you don't have to choose.
nancy.elementWhy: let the stories flow around you

together.text: Play telephone with the universe. Joel sends Nancy a made-up headline about the cabin. Nancy sends one back about the shore. Each must reply with a follow-up story as if it were real news. The Gemini moon is reading over both your shoulders.

title: The First Thin Smile
skyStory: There it is: the first thin smile of a new moon, six percent and grinning low in the west just after sunset. Gemini is still holding the microphone and won't give it back. The moon is practising introductions for its big month ahead. Hello, I'm the moon, I do tides. Mars applauds loudly. Saturn nods once, which for Saturn is a standing ovation.

reading: A waxing moon is the universe pressing the gas pedal very gently. Things you started this week will begin to show a little green. Resist the urge to dig them up and check the roots. The [[Ace of Pentacles]] is sitting on the cabin step, shaking its head at you.

Around midday, a wave of restlessness. The Tiger paces. Instead of starting something new, go outside for ten minutes and look for the first dandelion. There will be one, bold and too early, and you'll recognise yourself in it. Tell it good job. Then go back in and finish the thing you were doing.
joel.mission: Find the first dandelion of the season and send Nancy a photo of it with a dramatic one-word caption.
joel.omen: A sliver of moon visible while it's still light out. Your effort is showing before you think it is.

reading: Something small and new is starting in your corner of the world, and you're the first to see it. Maybe it's a habit, maybe a project, maybe just a better way to fold the towels. Whatever it is, it has your fingerprints all over it.

The [[Page of Pentacles]] reversed suggests you're tempted to wait until it's perfect before showing anyone. Show it anyway, at sixty percent. Someone will add the missing piece you didn't know you needed. This is how the Wood Rat builds empires: one clever, slightly unfinished thing at a time, passed hand to hand.
nancy.mission: Show one half-finished thing to someone today and ask them for exactly one suggestion.
nancy.omen: A chalk drawing on the sidewalk, half washed away by rain. Unfinished is beautiful; keep going.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's fire, for a fresh start
nancy.elementWhy: new things need a little heat

together.text: Find the moon tonight just after sunset, low in the west. Whoever spots it first sends the other one word describing its shape. Not banana. Anything but banana. Saturn has banned banana. The loser makes the first move on tomorrow's plans.

title: The Day of the Open Windows
skyStory: The moon has scuttled sideways into Cancer, the crab, carrying its thirteen percent of light like a shell it is not quite ready to leave. Cancer is the homebody of the zodiac and it wants every window in the hemisphere thrown open to let the winter out. Mars volunteers to do the heavy lifting. Saturn reminds everyone that screens exist for a reason.

reading: Today the cabin wants airing out. Open a window you haven't touched since October and let the stale winter air drift out like an old ghost that finally got the hint. The house will sound different afterward: birds, a lawnmower two streets over, a wind chime that has clearly never been tuned.

Home energy is strong, and so is the urge to fix everything inside it. Fix one hinge. One. The [[Four of Wands]] says the cabin is already a place worth coming back to, squeak and all. Tonight, sit somewhere you never sit in your own home and look at it the way a visitor would.
joel.mission: Open the most stubborn window in your home and leave it open for at least one full hour.
joel.omen: A wind chime ringing when you can't feel any breeze. Good news is on its way home to you.

reading: The crab moon is your friend today. It's patient, it protects what matters, and it walks sideways around obstacles instead of through them. You will too, all day, and everybody will wonder how you got where you are so fast.

Around 3:30 someone will lean on you for comfort, the steady-shoulder kind. Give it, of course. Then let them give something back, even if it's only a compliment you'd normally deflect. Today the mother of pearl wants you to say thank you and stop there. No but, no actually. Just thank you.
nancy.mission: Accept the next compliment you get with only the words thank you, then sip something to stop yourself adding more.
nancy.omen: A crab drawn in chalk on a sidewalk, walking sideways and grinning. You will get around today's obstacle without going through it.

together.text: Each of you choose one corner of your home to declare officially sunny, even if it's a windowsill and a cushion. Send a photo. These are now embassies. When either of you needs a moment, go stand in your embassy and think of the other one.

title: The First Day on the Clothesline
skyStory: Twenty-two percent and growing, the moon is still curled up in Cancer, which means it is folding laundry. Cosmic laundry. Clouds, mostly, and one comet it keeps pairing with the wrong sock. Mars offers to iron. Nobody lets Mars iron anymore, not since the incident with the nebula. Saturn hums quietly and matches corners with terrifying precision.

reading: First warm-ish breeze of May, and someone in your neighbourhood will hang laundry outside for the first time this year. Sheets snapping on a line. You'll feel it in your chest like a starting pistol. Summer has been announced, unofficially, by bedsheets.

Channel that into motion, but aim it. The [[Knight of Wands]] reversed keeps galloping off in four directions; today, rein it toward one task you've been dodging, the boring one with the long form. Finish it before 2 pm and reward yourself with a walk where you are not allowed to think about work. Just look at clotheslines.
joel.mission: Spot three clotheslines on your travels today and rate each one's laundry arrangement out of ten.
joel.omen: A single red sock on a line among white sheets. You're the bright spot in somebody's ordinary day.
joel.stoneWhy: a red sock in a white world

reading: The Wood Rat in you is nesting today, but strategically. Not a full clean, just one drawer, one shelf, one bag of things that clearly belong to another chapter. You'll find something in there you'd forgotten, small and shiny, and it will make you laugh out loud.

Take that as a hint from the moon: some of what you've been carrying can go. The [[Six of Swords]] is a boat, and boats float better lighter. Fill one bag. Put it by the door. Don't overthink where it goes next; that is tomorrow's question, and tomorrow is very capable.
nancy.mission: Clear out one drawer completely and keep only what makes you smile or what you actually used this year.
nancy.omen: A button found somewhere unexpected. Something small you lost is about to turn up exactly when you need it.

together.text: Each of you let go of one small thing today: a drawer of clutter, a grudge against a printer, an old to-do list. Text the other one word naming what you released. Respond only with a tiny salute. The crab moon will carry it off sideways.

title: The Half-Moon Hinge
skyStory: First quarter: the moon is lit down the middle like a cookie someone was too polite to finish. Still in Cancer, it is torn between staying in with blankets and going out to make something happen. This is the hinge of the month. Mars is jangling the car keys. Saturn has already packed a thermos and is waiting by the door, quietly ready for both.

reading: Half lit, half dark, and you'll feel both halves today. In the morning you'll want to build. In the afternoon you'll want to nap under a quilt. Both are correct. The trick is not to apologise to either one.

Somebody will push back on an idea of yours around 1 pm, gently but firmly. Instead of defending it like a castle, invite them inside and give them the tour. You'll find the weakest wall together and fix it in ten minutes. The [[Three of Pentacles]] is all about building with others, and you build best when you stop building alone.
joel.mission: Ask someone to poke holes in one of your ideas today, then thank them for each hole they find.
joel.omen: A door that won't quite latch. You're halfway between two things; that's okay, wedge it open.
joel.stoneWhy: solid ground for a hinge day

reading: The quarter moon asks one question: what are you willing to push for? For Nancy, the answer arrives before the question finishes. You know exactly which thing matters this month, and you've known since the snow melted.

Make one move on it today, a real one, not a planning move. Send the email. Book the call. Ask the question you've been rehearsing for a week. The Mountain is patient, but the Mountain also moves glaciers, and today a glacier gets a little nudge. Around 6, the shore will reward you with a sunset worth pulling over for.
nancy.mission: Do the one thing on your list that requires actual courage, and do it before your second cup of tea.
nancy.omen: Geese flying north in a ragged V. You're on course; the messy formation still gets there.
nancy.stoneWhy: a sharp edge for a decision

together.text: Halfway moon, halfway brave. Each of you name one small scary thing and do it by sundown. Report back with a single emoji of your choosing. If both are done, the cabin chimney and the shore both blink once tonight. Probably. Look closely.

title: The Day of the Two Lion Shirts
skyStory: The moon has strutted into Leo at forty-four percent, wearing sunglasses at night and expecting applause. Leo is the lion, the performer, the one who sings in grocery store aisles. Tonight it has arranged a small cosmic prank: two lions in two places at once. Mars thinks it's hilarious. Saturn checks the security footage and finds nothing. The lions are very good.

reading: A Leo moon is a big cat visiting a big cat, and the Fire Tiger is ready to purr. Your charm is turned up to eleven. People will laugh at jokes that are honestly only a seven. Enjoy it. You've earned an easy room.

Then, around 12:45, a stranger will walk past wearing a shirt covered in tiny lions. You'll laugh and send Nancy a photo. Within an hour she'll send one back: a different stranger, a different town, the same tiny lions. DES. The [[Strength]] card is grinning somewhere, gently holding a lion's jaw like it's a teacup.
joel.mission: Tell one joke today that you're not sure will land, and commit to it completely, including the pause.
joel.omen: A cat sunning itself on a car hood. Take your time; confidence is the slowest walk in the room.

reading: The Leo moon puts you on stage whether you signed up or not. Someone will ask you to explain something to a group, and your hands will take over like they've been waiting all week. People lean in. Somebody takes notes on a napkin.

Later, the lions arrive: a stranger on the sidewalk in a shirt full of them, just as Joel's message about his own lion shirt lands. Don't even scream. Well. Maybe one small scream into a scarf. The Wood Rat notes the time for the record, because the Wood Rat keeps records. It was 1:38.
nancy.mission: Explain something you love to someone who knows nothing about it, using your hands as much as possible.
nancy.omen: A lion statue outside a building you pass every day but never noticed. Look again at what's familiar.

together.text: Two lions, two towns, one ΔΕΣ. Celebrate it properly: each of you strike a ridiculous lion pose somewhere public-ish, a hallway or a parking lot, and send proof. Roars are optional but strongly encouraged by the moon.

title: The Day of the Borrowed Crown
skyStory: Over half lit now at fifty-five percent, the moon is still in Leo and has found a paper crown somewhere. It keeps adjusting it. Leo believes every evening is a coronation. Mars has been appointed royal fanfare. Saturn has been appointed royal treasurer and is already fretting about the crown's upkeep. The stars are just here for the party.

reading: Today someone will hand you a small leadership role you didn't ask for. Maybe it's choosing where everyone eats, maybe it's running a meeting when the usual person is away. Take the paper crown and wear it lightly. [[The Emperor]] reversed reminds you that ruling is mostly listening.

Your best move as monarch is to ask everyone else what they think first, then decide fast. Life Path 3 loves to talk, but today the crown sits better on a ruler who speaks last. Around 5, someone will thank you for making it easy. That's the whole job. Take the crown off at the cabin door and hang it on the coat hook.
joel.mission: In one conversation today, speak last instead of first, and notice what you learn by waiting.
joel.omen: A dog walking its owner, clearly in charge. Leading is knowing where you're going, not holding the leash.

reading: The Leo moon wants to give you something shiny and you'll want to refuse it. Don't. It could be praise, a gift of time, a seat by the window. The [[Nine of Cups]] reversed whispers that the wish isn't hollow at all if you let yourself actually enjoy it.

So enjoy it. Out loud. Say this is lovely and mean it. Around 4 pm, the light over the water will turn that particular spring gold that makes everything look like a painting. Stand in it for one minute. The Mountain is allowed to bask. Mountains bask constantly. It's half of what they do.
nancy.mission: Stand in the best patch of sunlight you can find for one full minute and do absolutely nothing useful.
nancy.omen: A golden retriever looking at you like you're the best thing that's happened all week. You are.

together.text: Tonight is a royal feast, the small kind. Each of you make a silly crown out of whatever's lying around: paper, foil, a pot lid. Wear it through dinner. Send a photo. The moon will judge the crowns and declare you both winners anyway.

title: The Great Spreadsheet of Spring
skyStory: The moon has slipped out of its Leo crown and into Virgo at sixty-six percent, and it immediately began alphabetising the constellations. Virgo is the editor of the zodiac. It notices typos in the Milky Way. Mars tries to help and is sent to sharpen pencils. Saturn and Virgo exchange a look of perfect understanding and start colour-coding the planets.

reading: Virgo moon energy will feel like wearing someone else's glasses: everything slightly too sharp. You'll notice every crooked picture frame, every email with a missing comma. Fix two. Then stop. The rest can stay charmingly crooked.

The [[Eight of Pentacles]] shows up at your workbench today, steady and focused. Pick one skill and practise it with care for twenty minutes, no shortcuts, no multitasking. The Fire Tiger can be a craftsman when it wants to be. Around 3:15 you'll slip into a little flow pocket and lose track of time. Let it happen.
joel.mission: Spend twenty uninterrupted minutes on one task, with your phone in another room, and time it.
joel.omen: A perfectly straight line of ants on the counter. Small, consistent effort is building something big.

reading: Here's a Virgo moon, and the Wood Rat is in heaven. Lists. Labels. A spreadsheet that finally makes sense. You'll spend a delightful hour organising something that nobody asked you to organise, and it will save three people a lot of fuss next month.

But watch for the Virgo trap: refining something that was already done. If you catch yourself on draft six, step away. The [[Queen of Pentacles]] says good enough is a gift you give your future self. Hand the thing in, then go outside and see if the first lilac buds have shown up yet. They're close. Tight little purple fists.
nancy.mission: Organise one small thing nobody asked you to, then don't mention it until someone discovers it.
nancy.omen: A perfectly folded paper airplane on the ground. Your careful work is about to travel further than expected.

together.text: Each of you pick one task you've been avoiding and set a timer for 25 minutes. Text go when you start, done when you finish. No other messages allowed in between. Virgo is timing you both and has a clipboard.

title: The Lilac Buds Are Watching
skyStory: Waxing gibbous, seventy-six percent, still in Virgo and still holding the clipboard. The moon is getting rounder and slightly smug about it. It has been checking on the lilac buds every night this week, measuring them with a tiny cosmic ruler. They are, it reports, on schedule. Mars wants them to bloom now. Saturn says lilacs answer to no one.

reading: Getting fuller, getting louder. Ideas will come thick and fast today, and the cabin's walls will be covered in sticky notes by sundown if you're not careful. Write them down, yes. But choose one to water. The rest can sit in the seed tray for now.

Around 10:30 a message will arrive asking for your help. Before you say yes, ask for something in return, even something tiny, like a coffee or a recommendation. The [[Six of Pentacles]] has been waiting all year for you to practise this. It will feel strange, like writing with your other hand. Do it anyway. The scales balance a little.
joel.mission: When someone asks you for a favour today, ask for one small thing back, out loud, and accept it gracefully.
joel.omen: A bird stealing string from a fence to build a nest. Taking what you need is how homes get built.

reading: The shore is thawing in earnest now. Tidal pools are warming up and something small and alive will catch your eye at the edge of the water or the edge of a puddle. A snail, a minnow, a beetle dressed for a wedding. Stop. Look closely. That's your Life Path 11 sending a postcard.

The message on the postcard: small things are paying attention. Today, the minor kindness you do without thinking, holding a door, remembering a name, is noticed by someone who needed it. You won't hear about it. That's fine. The [[Six of Swords]] crossing gets easier with every small kindness stacked in the boat.
nancy.mission: Learn the name of one person you see regularly but have never actually spoken to, and use it.
nancy.omen: A ladybug on your sleeve or windowsill. Something delicate is on its way; leave room for it.

together.text: Start a lilac watch. Each of you find one lilac bush near you and send a photo of its buds today. Repeat every few days. The first to send a full bloom wins bragging rights until June. Saturn will be adjudicating, slowly.

title: The Day of the Balanced Stones
skyStory: The moon has drifted into Libra at eighty-five percent and is trying to balance everything it owns on a single fingertip. Libra is the sign of scales, fairness and very long deliberations about which throw pillow goes where. Tonight the moon has arranged the planets in an elegant line. Mars nudges one. Everything wobbles. Saturn sighs and fixes it.

reading: A Libra moon wants fairness, and the Fire Tiger is about to get a lesson in it. Around 11, you'll notice you've been doing more than your share of something, again. Instead of quietly continuing, say it out loud, kindly. People are often happy to help. They just didn't know.

The [[Justice]] card stands at the edge of your day, holding its scales and raising an eyebrow. Balance doesn't mean doing less of what you love. It means letting other people do some of what they love too, and some of them love helping you. Imagine that. Tonight, let someone else pick the music.
joel.mission: Hand over one task you usually do yourself, and resist correcting how they do it.
joel.omen: Two birds sharing a feeder without squabbling. There's enough to go around; you don't have to grab.

reading: Today you'll be asked to settle something, a small dispute, a which-one-should-we-choose. Everyone trusts your judgement because you actually listen to both sides before deciding. The Wood Rat hears what isn't being said, too.

Make the call quickly and kindly, then let it go. Don't revisit it at 11 pm. The [[Two of Swords]] warns against blindfolding yourself with second thoughts. Later, if you can, find a beach or a riverbank and stack three stones into a little tower. It'll balance on the first try. Take a photo for Joel. He'll pretend he isn't impressed.
nancy.mission: Stack three stones into a tower somewhere outdoors and leave it there for a stranger to find.
nancy.omen: A seesaw perfectly level in an empty playground. Everything is in balance right now; enjoy the stillness.

together.text: Trade a puzzle. Each of you hand the other one small problem to think about for five minutes: Joel's goes to the shore, Nancy's goes to the cabin. Swap answers by dinner. Libra loves a fair exchange, and you two always see each other's blind spots.

title: The First Porch Evening
skyStory: Ninety-one percent and swelling, the moon lingers in Libra, polishing its scales until they shine. It is nearly full and knows it, the way a kettle knows it's nearly boiling. Tonight it's weighing two options: one more cold night, or the first proper warm evening of the year. Mars votes warm. Saturn abstains. The moon picks warm, barely.

reading: The first evening warm enough to sit outside without a blanket arrives tonight, or close enough to pretend. Drag a chair onto the porch or the step or the patch of grass by the cabin. Sit in it. That's the whole first assignment.

The second assignment is harder: let somebody bring you something while you sit there. A drink, a story, a second chair for themselves. The Tiger will want to jump up and host. Stay seated. [[The Sun]] reversed is sitting in the chair next to you, reminding you that joy does not need to be earned first.
joel.mission: Sit outside for fifteen minutes this evening without your phone, and let someone else do all the fetching.
joel.omen: The first moth bumping the porch light. Something is drawn to your glow; let it find you.

reading: Libra is asking you to weigh something that has been sitting on the scale too long, a small yes or no you keep postponing. Today the answer is obvious. You'll laugh at how long you held it, like finding your sunglasses on your head.

Then the evening opens up: soft air, the smell of thawed earth, someone's barbecue drifting across three yards. You'll want to walk down to the water. Go. The waves are rehearsing their summer set and could use an audience. Count seven waves, then make a small wish on the eighth. [[The Star]] reversed says your wishes are allowed to be simple.
nancy.mission: Walk to the nearest water, even a fountain, and make a wish on the eighth ripple or wave.
nancy.omen: Someone's porch light flicking on just as you pass. You're being welcomed somewhere new this month.

together.text: Both of you claim one outdoor chair tonight: porch, step or lawn. Sit at the same time, 8:30 pm, for ten minutes. Send one photo of your view, no words. The nearly full moon will be peeking over the treeline at both of you.

title: The Scorpio Full Moon Recharge
skyStory: The full moon has arrived, ninety-six percent and climbing, and it has chosen Scorpio, the most dramatic room in the house. Scorpio speaks in whispers and keeps secrets in velvet boxes. Tonight it holds the moon up like a lantern in a cave, revealing everything you tucked away in February. Mars leans in. Saturn takes off its glasses. Even the frogs go quiet.

reading: Full moon in Scorpio, and the Tiger feels everything twice as loud. An old feeling you thought you'd settled will drift back through, not to bother you, just to say hello and confirm the work you did. Nod at it. It'll leave on its own.

Tonight is the Full Moon Recharge. Take the onyx off your wrist and set it on a windowsill in the silver light, while Nancy sets the ruby beside her own moonlit window at the same time. Leave them out till morning. The [[Death]] card shows up reversed, not scary at all, just a door closing gently on a draft you no longer need.
joel.mission: Set the onyx on a windowsill in the moonlight tonight and leave it there until you wake up.
joel.omen: A light left on in an empty room. Something hidden is ready to be seen; look gently.

reading: The Wood Rat sees in the dark, but tonight the moon does it for you. Something you've half-known for a while becomes plainly obvious, like furniture appearing when the lights come on. It's not alarming. It's just clear, and clarity is a relief.

Set the ruby out for the Full Moon Recharge, cabochon facing up, purplish-pink catching all that silver. Text Joel when it's in place. Two windows, two stones, one moon doing the heavy lifting. The [[Six of Swords]] crossing feels shorter tonight, as if the far shore drifted a few metres closer while nobody was watching.
nancy.mission: Place the ruby on a moonlit windowsill tonight and text Joel the exact minute you set it down.
nancy.omen: An owl call after dark, or a picture of an owl. Your intuition is right; stop double-checking it.

together.text: Full Moon Recharge night. Set the ruby and onyx out at the same time, under the same moon, in two different windows. Then each of you whisper one thing you're done carrying. The Scorpio moon keeps secrets, so it's safe. Collect your stones at breakfast, freshly charged.

title: The Dog in Yellow Rain Boots
skyStory: Ninety-nine percent full and still brooding in Scorpio, the moon is in a mood for secrets and sly little reveals. It has been planning something all week, whispering to the wind and passing notes to the clouds. Tonight the punchline lands in two places at once. Mars spits out its tea. Saturn, for the first time in centuries, laughs out loud.

reading: At 2:22 this afternoon, give or take a minute, you'll see a dog wearing four tiny yellow rain boots, stepping around a puddle like a duke avoiding a moat. You'll stop. You'll stare. You'll send Nancy a photo, and her photo will arrive at the exact same moment: a different dog, a different town, the same tiny boots.

DES. There is no other response. The Scorpio moon is showing off, reminding you both that the threads between the cabin and the shore are tighter than anybody thinks. The rest of the day hums. Make one grand ruling about something small, like what to name the cabin's newest chair, and enjoy how easy it feels.
joel.mission: Name one object in your home today, officially, and tell someone its full name and title.
joel.omen: Any yellow thing at 2:22. The universe is winking at you, and it wants a wink back.
joel.stoneWhy: a sparkle for a shared joke

reading: The Scorpio moon has saved its best trick for you, and you'll get it in the middle of an ordinary errand. Keep your phone handy around 2:20. That's all the hint the moon is willing to give.

When it happens, when the dog in yellow rain boots trots past and Joel's matching photo lands in the same breath, don't even scream. Okay, scream a little. Then sit with it. Life Path 11 is about seeing connections other people miss, and today the connection is so loud even the gulls noticed. The [[Wheel of Fortune]] spins, and for once it's spinning just for fun.
nancy.mission: Take a photo of something yellow at exactly 2:22 pm and send it to Joel with no explanation.
nancy.omen: A gull laughing on a rooftop. It saw the boots too. Laugh back; joy is meant to be shared.
nancy.stoneWhy: the shore's stone for a shore day
nancy.elementWhy: puddles, boots and full moon tides

together.text: Tonight, write the official history of the Dog in Yellow Rain Boots. Joel writes the first sentence, Nancy writes the second, and you alternate until someone makes the other laugh out loud. File it under ΔΕΣ and never speak of it calmly again.

title: The Fullest Moon of Spring
skyStory: One hundred percent. The moon is completely, gloriously full, blazing in Sagittarius like an archer's target lit from within. Sagittarius is the wanderer, the one with a backpack always half-packed. Tonight the moon wants to go somewhere, anywhere, and it's calling every road in Atlantic Canada to come along. Mars has the map. Saturn has the snacks. Nobody has a plan, and that is the plan.

reading: A fire moon for a fire sign, and the Tiger is fully awake. You'll feel the itch to go somewhere new, even if it's just a different trail, a new coffee spot, a road you've never turned down. Turn down it. The Sagittarius moon rewards curiosity with tiny surprises.

But the [[Knight of Wands]] has one note: aim. Pick one direction and go all the way, instead of five half-trips. Tonight, set the onyx in the moonlight again, at the same hour Nancy's ruby faces the sky. The moon is fullest now, and the Full Moon Recharge works best when the two of you are thinking of each other at once.
joel.mission: Take a road, path or hallway you've never taken before and report the most surprising thing you find.
joel.omen: An arrow painted on pavement pointing somewhere unexpected. Follow your gut; it's aiming true tonight.
joel.stoneWhy: a second night in the moonlight
joel.elementWhy: fire moon, fire sign, Fire Tiger

reading: The full moon is fattest tonight and it's shining straight down on your path like a spotlight that finally got the cue right. Something you've worked toward quietly for months gets a moment of recognition. Small, maybe, but unmistakable.

[[The Sun]] reversed asks you to stop earning the joy and just allow it. When someone says well done, the correct response is a grin, not a list of everything you still need to fix. Then the ruby goes back on the windowsill for one more night of moon charging. Tomorrow it'll glow a little brighter on your pinky.
nancy.mission: When someone praises you today, respond only with a grin and the word yes. Nothing else. See how it feels.
nancy.omen: A balloon floating free in the sky. Something you've been holding tight wants to rise; let it.
nancy.stoneWhy: one more night under the full moon

together.text: The moon is completely full. Set the ruby and onyx out once more and step outside at 9:45, wherever you are. Raise one hand to the moon like you're toasting it. It's the fullest it will be all spring, and it came out just for you two.

title: The Long Weekend Launch
skyStory: Ninety-eight percent and barely dimmed, the moon is still roaming Sagittarius with its boots untied. It is the Friday before a long weekend, and the moon can feel it. Everyone's packing coolers, digging out lawn chairs, checking the forecast seventeen times. Mars has already loaded the car. Saturn quietly double-checks the tire pressure, because somebody has to.

reading: Long weekend energy hits you around 3 pm like a gust off the bay. Suddenly everything is a plan: the cabin, a campfire, a hike, the very first marshmallow of the season. The Fire Tiger wants to do all of it, simultaneously, by Sunday.

Pick two. Write them down. Tell someone. The [[Eight of Wands]] is all arrows flying at once, which is beautiful but exhausting, so choose which two arrows matter. Then, tonight, collect the onyx from the windowsill. Feel the weight of it, cool and charged. Put it back on your left wrist and let it hold the weekend steady.
joel.mission: Write your two long-weekend plans on a scrap of paper and stick it to the fridge with your best magnet.
joel.omen: A woodpile stacked neatly by a stranger's shed. Preparation now means easy fires later; do one small prep task.
joel.stoneWhy: freshly charged and back on the wrist
joel.elementWhy: steady plans for a wild weekend

reading: The Sagittarius moon is pulling at your sleeve, asking you to wander a little this weekend. Not far. Just somewhere new enough that your eyes have to work. A beach you haven't walked in years, a trail with a funny name, a town with one stoplight.

You'll want to plan it perfectly. Don't. Pick a direction and leave room for detours, because the best moment will be one you didn't schedule: a fiddler on a porch, a heron standing perfectly still in the shallows, an ice cream stand that just opened for the season. [[The Fool]] is skipping ahead of you, waving.
nancy.mission: Plan a small weekend outing with exactly one fixed point and leave everything else to chance.
nancy.omen: A road sign for a town you've never heard of. Write the name down; it's a future adventure.

together.text: Long weekend kickoff. Each of you send the other a three-word plan for the weekend, no more, no less. Then on Monday, send three words describing how it actually went. The gap between the two is where all the good stories live.

title: The Day of the Smoky Hoodie
skyStory: Waning gibbous now, ninety-five percent, the moon has started its slow exhale. It's still in Sagittarius and still in a travelling mood, but it's taking the scenic route home. Tonight it hangs over every first campfire of the season like a nosy neighbour. Mars stokes the flames. Saturn sits upwind, wisely, with a blanket over its knees.

reading: First campfire of the year, if the weather cooperates, and the Fire Tiger is in its element. Literally. You'll build the fire perfectly, of course, and you'll want everyone to know it. Let them know it. Then hand someone else the poker.

Somewhere around the second log, conversation will turn deep in the way it only does around flames. Someone will tell you something real. Listen with your whole face. The [[Ten of Wands]] reversed says you don't have to carry their story for them; just hold it for a minute, then let the smoke take it up. Your hoodie will smell like woodsmoke for days. That's a feature.
joel.mission: Build or sit beside a fire tonight, even a candle, and tell one story you've never told before.
joel.omen: An ember drifting upward and winking out among the stars. Ideas don't need to last forever to light the way.

reading: The storyteller's night has arrived. When the fire settles and the faces turn orange, everyone will look at you. Your hands know what to do. Tell the one about the time you got lost and found something better.

The Wood Rat is clever enough to know when to stop: right at the best part, so they beg for more. Leave them hanging. Save the ending for tomorrow. The [[Page of Wands]] is sitting cross-legged in the front row, mouth open. Later, wrap yourself in the smokiest blanket and look up. The moon has shrunk by a whisker, but it's still bright enough to read by.
nancy.mission: Tell a story tonight and stop right before the ending. Promise to finish it tomorrow, then actually do.
nancy.omen: A log that suddenly flares up when you thought the fire was out. An old idea of yours has life in it yet.

together.text: Campfire summit. If either of you has a fire, a candle, or even a flashlight under a blanket, send a photo of the glow tonight. The other replies with a one-line ghost story, the less scary the better. Saturn's is about a chair that squeaks.

title: The Moon Climbs Nancy's Mountain
skyStory: Here comes the moon, ninety percent full, hiking straight into Capricorn, Nancy's own sign. It arrives with sensible boots, a thermos and a deep respect for elevation. Capricorn is the mountain goat, steady on cliffs that make everyone else dizzy. Saturn, who rules Capricorn, has tidied the whole summit. There are fresh towels. There is a welcome mat. Mars wipes its feet for once.

reading: The moon is visiting Nancy's sign, and the cabin feels it as a kind of quiet steadiness. You'll find yourself finishing things today instead of starting them. Your inner Capricorn neighbour has come over and is helping you clean the gutters, metaphorically.

Use the Capricorn moon to build something that lasts: fix the wobbly step, finally label the toolbox, write down how you like the cabin set up for summer. Around 4 pm, switch the onyx to your right wrist and send Nancy a jolt of strength. It's her moon. She's earned some extra wind in her sails.
joel.mission: Switch the onyx to your right wrist this afternoon to send Nancy strength, and tell her you did.
joel.omen: Anything that climbs steadily: a squirrel, a vine, a slow cyclist. Slow climbing wins the summit.

reading: Presents have arrived on the mountain: the moon is in your sign, and it delivered them personally. You'll feel taller today, steadier, as if the mountain inside you got a fresh coat of snow on its peak and a sunrise to show it off.

Something you've been pushing uphill finally reaches a ledge where you can rest and look back. Look back. See how far you've come. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed reminds you not to turn this into another reason to work harder; stand on the ledge and enjoy the view. This afternoon you'll feel a little jolt of warmth near your pinky. That's Joel switching wrists.
nancy.mission: Find the highest point near you, a hill, a staircase or a lookout, and stand on it for two minutes looking out.
nancy.omen: Your ruby catching the light at an angle you've never noticed. Strength is arriving from across the distance.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's stone, glowing with sent strength

together.text: The moon is in Nancy's sign. Today Joel sends strength by switching his onyx to the right wrist, and Nancy confirms receipt by holding up her pinky like a toast. Send each other a photo of the gesture. The mountain hears, and so does the cabin.

title: The Day of the First Planting
skyStory: Still in Capricorn at eighty-four percent, the moon has rolled up its sleeves and joined the great long weekend planting. Half of Atlantic Canada is on its knees in the garden, and the other half is warning them about frost. The moon sides with the planters. Saturn, ruler of the goat, quietly checks the forecast anyway. Mars has already planted something upside down.

reading: Your hands want to be in the dirt today, and the Capricorn moon agrees. Plant something, anything: a single tomato seedling, a pot of herbs, a sunflower seed pushed into the soil with your thumb. The Fire Tiger digging is a sight to behold, and also slightly chaotic.

Here's the deal with seeds. You can't make them grow faster by watching. The [[Seven of Pentacles]] reminds you that good things take a whole season. So plant, water, and walk away. Tonight, sit by the cabin with dirt under your nails and a sense of having done exactly enough. That feeling is rarer than it should be. Notice it.
joel.mission: Plant one seed, seedling or bulb today, and give it a name worthy of a fantasy novel hero.
joel.omen: An earthworm surfacing right where you're digging. You're in the right spot; keep going.
joel.stoneWhy: a seed of light in dark soil

reading: Another day of moon in your sign, and you're on a roll. People come to you with questions, and you somehow have every answer. It's not magic. It's years of noticing. The Wood Rat has been taking notes since before anyone else woke up.

Take a minute before lunch to watch your hands while you talk. Watch them dance. Five stones, five elements, every one catching light: onyx for earth, ruby for fire, mother of pearl for water, diamonds for wind, and the ruby again for heart. Together they summon something no single ring could. The [[Queen of Wands]] approves of every sparkle.
nancy.mission: Tell one story today and deliberately count how many different gestures your hands make while you tell it.
nancy.omen: A rainbow caught in a garden sprinkler. All five elements are lining up for you today.
nancy.elementWhy: the fifth element ties it all

together.text: Plant something today, both of you, then send the other a photo of the spot where it's buried. No seedlings visible, just dirt. Agree to check back in three weeks with progress photos. Whoever sprouts first gets to name the other's plant.

title: The Day of the Odd Invention
skyStory: The moon has floated into Aquarius at seventy-seven percent, and it has brought a box of spare parts. Aquarius is the inventor of the zodiac, the one who builds a bird feeder out of a colander and calls it art. Tonight the moon is tinkering with the tides, trying to make them run sideways. Mars hands it tools. Saturn reads the warranty.

reading: Aquarius moon plus a builder's brain equals one gloriously strange idea before lunch. Maybe a shelf that folds into a bench. Maybe a new way of sorting the cabin's mystery-key drawer. It will sound ridiculous out loud. Say it out loud anyway.

Then find one person who thinks it's brilliant and one who thinks it's bonkers, and listen to both. The [[Page of Swords]] loves a fresh idea but wants you to test it before you build it. Sketch it on the back of an envelope. Leave the envelope somewhere visible. Next week, you'll look at it and know.
joel.mission: Sketch one odd invention on the back of an envelope and leave it pinned somewhere you'll see daily.
joel.omen: A machine making an unusual noise that turns out to be fine. Weird isn't broken; sometimes it's brilliant.

reading: The Wood Rat has always been a little bit Aquarius at heart: clever, unconventional, quietly three steps ahead. Today that streak comes out to play. You'll solve a stubborn problem using a method nobody else would have tried, and it'll work on the first go.

Somebody will ask how you thought of it. Tell them the truth, which is that you noticed something odd last Tuesday and kept it in your pocket until it was useful. That's the whole secret of the Wood Rat. [[The Magician]] reversed reminds you that every tool is already on the table. You don't need a new one. You need the weird one.
nancy.mission: Solve one ordinary problem today in the strangest way that still works, and tell Joel how you did it.
nancy.omen: A piece of string tied in a bow on a fence post. A small, clever fix is waiting for you to notice it.
nancy.stoneWhy: grounding for a flighty, clever day

together.text: Invention swap: each of you describe one ridiculous gadget that would make the other's day easier. Joel's must involve the shore. Nancy's must involve the cabin. Patents pending. The Aquarius moon will build none of them but applauds the vision.

title: The Day of the Cosmic Broom
skyStory: Last quarter, sixty-eight percent, and the moon is lit down one side like a face turning away from the camera. It is still in Aquarius, still tinkering, but now it's taking things apart instead of building them. Most of the month is behind it. Mars wants to keep going. Saturn says every good builder spends time sweeping up the sawdust.

reading: A waning quarter moon is a broom, and today the Tiger is holding it. Look at all the half-started things scattered around you: tabs, notes, projects with names but no second step. Choose three to keep. Thank the rest and let them go.

This will feel almost impossible, because every idea is your favourite child. But the [[Knight of Wands]] reversed has been warning you all month, and it's not mad, just tired. Aim the fire. Archive the rest. Around 4:10, you'll feel lighter, like finally kicking off winter boots in May.
joel.mission: Close every tab or note you haven't touched in a week, and keep only the three that still excite you.
joel.omen: A bin by the curb, full and ready for pickup. Letting go is a chore, but it makes room for something new.

reading: Half moon on the wane, and you're in sorting mode, but a gentler kind than usual. Not a purge, a review. You'll look back over the last few weeks and see a pattern you missed while you were in it, a thread of good decisions running right through the middle.

Name the thread out loud, even just to yourself in the car. It's the [[Six of Swords]] showing you how much water has already passed under the boat. Then drop one small worry overboard, something you've been chewing on since April. Watch it sink. The Mountain keeps the lessons and lets the rest go with the tide.
nancy.mission: Write down three good decisions you made this month, and read them aloud to yourself before bed.
nancy.omen: Driftwood washed up perfectly smooth. Time and water have softened something that used to be rough.
nancy.elementWhy: a small flame for old worries

together.text: The month is turning. Each of you write one thing you're bringing into June and one thing you're leaving in May. Swap lists by text. Then promise to remind each other of the first and never mention the second again.

title: The Lilac Photo Collision
skyStory: Fifty-nine percent and fading, the moon is lingering in Aquarius, where it has been running experiments on coincidence. Its latest hypothesis: if two friends watch two lilac bushes long enough, the bushes will start coordinating. Tonight it publishes the results. Mars reads the paper upside down. Saturn peer-reviews it and finds no errors, which is deeply suspicious.

reading: This morning, your lilac watch ends. The bush you've been tracking finally opens, all at once, purple and ridiculous and smelling like every spring at once. You'll take a photo at 8:41 and hit send. Nancy's photo will arrive at 8:41 too. Same minute. Both bushes with one single white blossom tucked among the purple.

DES. Somewhere, the Aquarius moon is high-fiving itself. The rest of the day will run on that strange, fizzy feeling, as if the universe is leaning closer to listen. Use it. Say the encouraging thing you were going to save for later. The [[Three of Cups]] wants friends celebrating together, even across the miles between the cabin and the shore.
joel.mission: Bring one sprig of lilac, or any flower, indoors and put it somewhere you'll pass a dozen times today.
joel.omen: A single white blossom among purple ones. You and Nancy are more in tune than any clock.
joel.elementWhy: lilacs rooted and blooming on cue

reading: The lilac watch reaches its finale this morning, and you'll win, and so will Joel, at the exact same minute. Two photos crossing in the air at 8:41, two bushes blooming on cue, each hiding one rogue white flower like a secret signature.

Don't even scream. Actually, do. The Wood Rat in you will immediately start building theories, and that's half the fun. The other half is simply letting it be magic. Life Path 11 doesn't need an explanation. Spend the afternoon with the window open so the lilac smell can find you. Tell someone the story tonight. Watch them squint, then grin.
nancy.mission: Smell a lilac today, deeply and theatrically, with your eyes closed, as if judging a competition.
nancy.omen: Two of anything, side by side, perfectly matched. The universe is reminding you that you're never solo.
nancy.stoneWhy: a sparkle for a sparkling coincidence

together.text: Two lilac bushes, one minute, one white blossom each. ΔΕΣ, officially. Tonight, each of you set a sprig of lilac beside your stone, the onyx and the ruby, and send a photo. The Aquarius moon has asked for a copy for its records.

title: The Great Coastal Fog
skyStory: Exactly half lit, the moon has drifted out of Aquarius and into Pisces, where everything goes soft at the edges. Fog rolls in off the water like a giant cat stretching across the coast. The moon can't see a thing and loves it. Mars keeps bumping into constellations. Saturn has turned on its fog lights and is driving extremely slowly.

reading: Morning fog, the thick coastal kind, and the Tiger can't see three steps ahead. Good. Today isn't a day for plans. It's a day for the next step only. Take it. Then the next. By lunch you'll be somewhere better than you would have planned.

The fog is also a gentle cover for receiving. Nobody can see you being looked after today, so let someone do it: a coworker covering a task, a friend dropping off something you mentioned once. The [[Six of Pentacles]] reversed has been patient all month. Today, finally, you receive without keeping score. The fog keeps your secret.
joel.mission: Walk somewhere in the fog, or pretend you are, and notice three sounds that seem closer than they are.
joel.omen: A foghorn, or any long low sound. You're on course; keep going slowly and steadily.

reading: Fog suits you, secretly. The Wood Rat navigates by whisker and memory, and you know every turn of your day without needing to see it. While everyone else is squinting, you'll glide.

The Pisces moon softens your edges too, and something you've been firm about all month can relax just slightly. Not give in. Just soften. The [[Eight of Swords]] reversed reveals the blindfold was never tied; you can take it off whenever you like. Around 7 pm the fog lifts in one sudden sweep, and the shore appears all at once, sparkling, like it's been waiting for you to look up.
nancy.mission: Let one small rule you hold yourself to slide today, and notice that nothing at all falls apart.
nancy.omen: A bird singing in the fog where you can't see it. Help is closer than it looks; just ask.
nancy.stoneWhy: earth to stand on in the mist

together.text: Fog day. Neither of you needs to do anything impressive. Send each other one photo of something soft: a blanket, a cloud, a cat, a sweater sleeve. The prize for the softest photo is an extra-long nap, awarded by the Pisces moon personally.

title: The Day of the Beach Glass
skyStory: Forty percent and slimming, the moon is still paddling in Pisces, combing the beaches for treasure. It collects sea glass the way Saturn collects rules: obsessively, and in matching jars. Tonight it has found a piece the exact colour of Nancy's ruby. Mars wants to keep it. The moon says finders keepers, then quietly leaves it on the shore for her.

reading: Pisces moon, end of May, and the cabin feels like a lighthouse keeper's cottage today. Steady light, steady rhythm. People will drift toward you for a word of encouragement, and you'll have exactly the right one ready, sharpened by a month of practice.

Here's the twist: you'll be offered encouragement in return, from someone you don't expect, maybe the quietest person in the room. Catch it. Hold it like a piece of beach glass, smooth and a little bit magic. The [[Page of Cups]] reversed reminds you that the soft gifts are the ones that last. Put it in your pocket, metaphorically. Then literally, if it's glass.
joel.mission: Write down a compliment someone gave you this month on a small card and keep it in your coat pocket.
joel.omen: A smooth stone or bit of glass on a path. A rough thing in your life is quietly getting smoother.

reading: If you can get to the shore today, go. The tide will be low around mid-afternoon and the beach will be scattered with glass: green, white, brown, and one rare piece of purplish-pink that looks suspiciously like your ruby. The Pisces moon left it for you.

Even if you can't get there, the feeling finds you. A small, unexpected gift arrives: a kind message, an old photo, a forgotten treasure in a coat pocket. The [[Six of Cups]] is all about gentle memories and simple gifts. Accept it without wondering if you deserve it. You do. The shore always gives back what you give it.
nancy.mission: Go looking for one small treasure today, sea glass, a whelk shell or a heart-shaped pebble, and bring it home.
nancy.omen: A piece of purplish-pink anything. Joel is thinking about you, and the ruby agrees.
nancy.stoneWhy: glass and pearl, both shaped by sea

together.text: Treasure swap. Each of you find one small natural thing today, a stone, a shell, a leaf, and describe it to the other in exactly ten words. No photos until tomorrow. Guess what it looks like. Saturn will compare the guesses to the real thing.

title: The Tiger Gets a Return Visit
skyStory: The moon has slimmed to thirty percent and wandered back into Aries, Joel's sign, for the second time this month. It remembers the crackers. It remembers where the cabin key is hidden. It lets itself in, puts its feet up by the stove and asks what Joel has been up to since the third. Mars brings out the photo album. Saturn sends a slightly warmer postcard this time.

reading: The moon is back in your sign, and it wants a progress report. Look at the idea you folded under the onyx on the third of May. Unfold it. You'll be surprised: you did more of it than you thought, and the parts you didn't do have quietly stopped mattering.

That's the Aries lesson this time around. Not more fire, but better-aimed fire. The [[Knight of Wands]] finally lowers its lance and nods. Celebrate with something small and Tiger-ish: a fast walk, a loud song, a burst of making that lasts exactly one hour. Then stop on purpose, satisfied. Leave the second hour for tomorrow.
joel.mission: Find the idea note from May 3, or write one now, and tell Nancy one thing you did about it this month.
joel.omen: A red bird landing nearby. Your fire has been noticed; keep it aimed and steady.
joel.elementWhy: the moon is back in Aries

reading: With the moon back in Joel's sign, you get to cheer from the shore again, and you're very good at cheering. The Wood Rat sees exactly what Joel did this month that he hasn't noticed himself. Tell him. Specifically. He'll deflect. Tell him again.

Then turn the same sharp eye on yourself. The Mountain moved this month, a little, in a direction you chose. [[The World]] reversed hints that one cycle is nearly complete but wants a proper ending, not a fade-out. Name what you finished. Write it in your neatest handwriting. Put it somewhere it can be seen.
nancy.mission: Tell Joel one specific thing he did well this month, then insist he accepts it with no deflecting.
nancy.omen: A line chalked across a driveway. One chapter is complete; step over it with a little hop.

together.text: Joel's turn to receive. Nancy sends him one compliment, specific and true, and Joel must reply only with thank you, no deflections, no jokes. If he cracks, he owes the moon a bow. Then swap, and Nancy plays by the same rules.

title: The Last Night of May
skyStory: Twenty-one percent and fading gently, the moon spends the last night of May still curled up in Aries, warming its hands at the cabin stove. It's been a big month: frogs, lilacs, fog, a dog in yellow boots. The moon is writing it all down in a tiny silver notebook. Mars wants a sequel. Saturn says June will be busy enough without one.

reading: May is closing its door softly behind you. Somewhere a lawnmower is running its first long evening route, the lilacs are already dropping petals, and summer is leaning on the gate. The cabin chimney sends up one last thin curl of smoke for the season, a small goodbye.

Before bed, take a moment to put the onyx on your left wrist and leave it there. Receiving side. All month, the [[Six of Pentacles]] has tried to teach you that being given to is part of the deal. Tonight, receive the evening itself: the cool air, the stars, the quiet. You don't owe it anything. It's just yours.
joel.mission: Spend five minutes outside tonight listing out loud everything good that happened in May, counting on your fingers.
joel.omen: A late bird singing after dark. One last gift from May, wishing you a bright June.
joel.elementWhy: a warm wind carrying you into June

reading: The last night of May finds you somewhere near the water, if only in your head: the shore at dusk, the tide coming in slow, the first warm breeze that smells like salt and cut grass. It's the season turning, and you're right on time.

Look back over the month and count your crossings. The [[Six of Swords]] boat has moved further than you think, and Joel has been rowing too. Take the ruby off your pinky for a moment, hold it to the last of the light, and put it back on. The Mountain is ready for June. June has no idea what's coming.
nancy.mission: Hold the ruby up to the last light of the day for ten seconds, then send Joel one word for June.
nancy.omen: The first firefly, or something that glows like one. Summer is close, and so is good news.
nancy.stoneWhy: Joel's stone, held up to the light

together.text: May is over. Each of you choose your favourite moment of the month, the lions, the boots, the lilacs, or something nobody else knows about, and send it to the other in one sentence. Then decide together on one word for June. Saturn will hold you to it.
